paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus brings the good stuff when the supply runs out. The wine is gone, the party is stuck, and nobody at that wedding has a fix. Then Jesus tells the servants, "Fill the jars with water," and the water becomes wine (John 2:7, 9). When you hit the bottom of your own supply, that's not the end, because it's right where He shows up.

Look at who sees it, though. The master of the banquet "did not know where it was from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew" (John 2:9). The servants just did what they were told, and they got the front-row seat. I think that's a gift for any baker who does the small, plain job in front of them. Trusting Jesus and doing what He says puts you right where the miracle happens.

And the master says it best: "you have saved the fine wine until now!" (John 2:10). Jesus doesn't hand out leftovers. John calls this "the first of His signs," and says it "revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him" (John 2:11). So the point is bigger than a party getting rescued. The sign shows who Jesus is, and that's why you can trust Him with whatever you've run out of.
